newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Tri Polyta to up investment in Nisshoku.
newsitem.headline: Tri Polyta to up investment in Nisshoku.

text.p: Indonesian petrochemical giant PT Tri Polyta Indonesia said on Friday it planned to increase its investment in joint venture acrylic acid producer PT Nisshoku Tripolyta Acrylindo (NTA).

"Tri Polyta plans to increase its investment in NTA, a joint venture company between Nippon Shokubai Co (50 percent), Tri Polyta (45 percent) and Tomen Corporation (five percent)," Tri Polyta said in a statement.
Tri Polyta said the firm planned to increase its investment in NTA to 63.342 billion rupiah, or 27 million shares, from 26.392 billion rupiah, or 11.25 million shares.
Tri Polyta, Indonesia's biggest producer of polypropylene resins, is also listed in New York.
Polypropylene resins are a type of plastics used to manufacture a wide range of consumer products such as carpets, rope and automobile parts.
Tri Polyta said NTA will be the first acrylic acid and ester producer in Indonesia and would distribute its products in the domestic and international market.
Acrylic ester is a material commonly used in the painting industry.
It said NTA's shareholders planned to increase NTA's total issued and paid capital to 140.76 billion rupiah, or 60 million shares, from 58.65 billion rupiah, or 25 million shares.
Nippon Shokubai planned increase its investment to 70.38 billion rupiah, or 30 million shares, from 29.325 billion rupiah, or 12.5 million shares, it said.
Tomen planned to increase its investment to 7.038 billion rupiah, or three million shares, from 2.932 billion rupiah, or 1.25 million shares.
The stakes of each partner in NTA would however remain the same, it said.
Tri Polyta said it believed the increase of investment in NTA would provide better returns to the firm.

Tri Polyta said NTA was expected to capitalise on the possibility that Japan would reduce its domestic production levels and would expand and build joint venture acrylic ester factories outside of Japan.
Japan is currently the main supplier of acrylic ester in Southeast Asia, it said.
Tri Polyta said 60 percent of its total project investment of around $154 million was expected to be financed by long term borrowings and the remaining by equity funding.
It said it planned to hold an extraordinary shareholders meeting on November 11 to seek approvals for the planned increase.
